title: Tucker's Lemma at n = 2: a Complementary Edge Always Exists on the Hexagon Disk
description: The sperner-mathlib4-oq-02 program has, over sixteen iterations, machine-checked every STRUCTURAL piece of the door-counting proof of Tucker's lemma: the abstract path-following / handshaking engines (SpernerTuckerPathFollowing, SpernerTuckerDoorGraph, SpernerTuckerDoorIncidenceParity, SpernerTuckerInductiveTower), the fact that the concrete n = 2 hexagon DOOR GRAPH is paths-and-cycles (hdoor + hsimplex in SpernerTuckerHexagonFullDoorGraph / SpernerTuckerHexagonPseudomanifold), and the odd oriented BOUNDARY SEED (SpernerTuckerHexagonSignDegree, SpernerTuckerSignDegreeOneDim). Every one of those is a statement about the MACHINERY — door incidence bounds, degree sequences, the sign-degree seed — never Tucker's actual CONCLUSION. Tucker's lemma itself asserts something simpler and stronger: for an antipodally-labelled triangulation of B², there is a COMPLEMENTARY EDGE — an edge whose two endpoints carry antipodal labels {k, −k}. That conclusion had never been stated, let alone proved, for a concrete n = 2 triangulation in this program. This entry supplies it. On the standard hexagon + centre triangulation of B² (seven vertices: six boundary vertices v₀…v₅ on ∂B² = S¹ labelled antipodally v_{i+3} = −v_i from three free labels a,b,c, plus one interior centre vertex with a FREE label d; twelve edges: six spokes centre–vᵢ and six boundary edges vᵢ–v_{i+1} cyclic; labels in {+1,+2,−1,−2} as Fin 4 with negL = [2,3,0,1]), tucker_hexagon proves by kernel decide over all 4⁴ = 256 antipodal labellings that a complementary edge always exists — either a spoke (d = negL vᵢ) or a boundary edge (v_{i+1} = negL vᵢ). Crucially the result is genuinely 2-dimensional: boundary_ring_insufficient exhibits an antipodal labelling of the six boundary vertices under which NO boundary edge is complementary (24 of the 64 boundary labellings), so Tucker here does NOT reduce to the already-verified 1-D (S¹) statement; and interior_spoke_rescues shows that whenever the boundary ring carries no complementary edge, a spoke to the centre is complementary for EVERY centre label d — the concrete n = 1 → n = 2 step, the boundary (an n = 1 Tucker instance on the arc) failing on the ring being repaired by the interior cone over it. Honest status: a concrete verification for one coarse triangulation by exhaustive kernel evaluation, not a dimension-free proof — that remains the abstract path-following program's job. Its value is orthogonal to the engine files: the first time the ACTUAL Tucker conclusion (a complementary edge, the object Borsuk–Ulam ultimately consumes) is machine-checked at n = 2, and the first proof in the program that the n = 2 statement is not a disguised n = 1 one. 0 axioms, 0 sorries (propext / Quot.sound only — plain decide, no Lean.ofReduceBool).

overview.historicalContext: Tucker's lemma (Albert W. Tucker, 1945) is the combinatorial heart of the Borsuk–Ulam theorem: for an antipodally symmetric triangulation of the n-ball Bⁿ with a labelling λ into {±1,…,±n} that is antipodal on the boundary sphere, some edge is complementary (its two endpoints carry labels k and −k). The constructive proofs (Freund–Todd 1981; Prescott–Su 2005) follow a path along the almost-complementary simplices from a forced boundary endpoint to an interior complementary one — the door-counting argument the parent problem sperner-mathlib4-oq-02 formalizes abstractly. Sixteen prior iterations of that program verified the abstract engines (path-following, incidence parity, the TuckerTower dimension recursion), showed the concrete hexagon door graph is paths-and-cycles, and identified the odd oriented boundary seed as a hemisphere sign-degree. What none of them stated is Tucker's own conclusion on a concrete triangulation: that a complementary edge exists. This entry closes that gap for the standard hexagon + centre triangulation of B².
overview.problemStatement: On the hexagon + centre triangulation of B² — six boundary vertices v₀…v₅ labelled antipodally (v_{i+3} = negL v_i, from three free labels a,b,c on v₀,v₁,v₂) and one interior centre vertex with a free label d, labels in {+1,+2,−1,−2} encoded as Fin 4 with negL = ![2,3,0,1] — prove that for every one of the 4⁴ = 256 antipodal labellings there is a complementary edge: either a spoke centre–vᵢ with d = negL vᵢ, or a boundary edge vᵢ–v_{i+1} (cyclic) with v_{i+1} = negL vᵢ. Prove further that the result is genuinely two-dimensional: exhibit a boundary labelling under which no boundary edge is complementary, and prove that in every such case a spoke rescues the complementary edge for every centre label d.
overview.proofStrategy: Everything is a finite check discharged by kernel decide (not native_decide, so no Lean.ofReduceBool). The labels form Fin 4 and the vertices Fin 6; negL, the antipodal boundary condition (V a b c is ![a,b,c,negL a,negL b,negL c]), the spoke predicate spokeCompl (∃ i, d = negL (V a b c i)) and the boundary predicate boundaryCompl (∃ i, V a b c (i+1) = negL (V a b c i)) are all decidable. tucker_hexagon reverts the four label variables and decides spokeCompl ∨ boundaryCompl over all 256 labellings; exists_complementary_edge just unfolds the two predicates. boundary_ring_insufficient decides ∃ a b c, ¬ boundaryCompl a b c (a witness where the ring has no complementary edge). interior_spoke_rescues decides ∀ a b c d, ¬ boundaryCompl a b c → spokeCompl a b c d. The Fin-indexed existentials over ![…] vectors reduce cheaply in the kernel, keeping the decide well inside memory limits.
keyInsights: The program had verified the entire door-counting MACHINERY at n = 2 (the door graph is paths-and-cycles, the sign-degree seed is odd) but never Tucker's own CONCLUSION — that a complementary edge exists — on a concrete triangulation. This entry supplies that conclusion directly, by exhaustive kernel evaluation, orthogonally to the engine files.

The result is genuinely 2-dimensional, not a disguised 1-D fact: on 24 of the 64 antipodal boundary labellings the hexagon RING carries no complementary edge, so the already-verified 1-D (S¹) Tucker does not by itself produce the edge — the interior centre vertex is essential.

The interior does exactly the missing work: whenever the boundary ring has no complementary edge, a spoke to the centre is complementary for EVERY centre label d. This is the concrete n = 1 → n = 2 cone step — the boundary being an n = 1 Tucker instance on the antipodal ring, and its failure on the ring being repaired by the interior cone over it.

The whole verification is 0-axiom (propext / Quot.sound only, no Classical.choice, no native_decide): plain kernel decide over Fin-indexed existentials keeps the exhaustive 256-labelling search inside the kernel's trusted reduction, so the concrete Tucker conclusion is machine-checked without the Lean.ofReduceBool trust extension.

tucker_hexagon and exists_complementary_edge are definitionally the same fact stated two ways: the former packages it behind the named predicates spokeCompl/boundaryCompl, the latter unfolds it to the raw existential over vertex indices that a downstream Borsuk–Ulam corollary would pattern-match on to extract an actual edge — a deliberate split between the internal abstraction and the concrete witness a consumer needs.

sections.title: From the Door-Counting Machinery to Tucker's Actual Conclusion
sections.summary: The header frames the entry against sixteen iterations of the sperner-mathlib4-oq-02 program: every prior file verified a piece of the door-counting MACHINERY (path-following engines, the hexagon door graph is paths-and-cycles, the odd sign-degree seed) but never Tucker's own CONCLUSION — that a complementary edge exists — on a concrete triangulation. It states the hexagon + centre model of B² (seven vertices, twelve edges, {±1,±2} labels as Fin 4 with negL = [2,3,0,1]) and lists the four results: tucker_hexagon (a complementary edge always exists), its existential form, boundary_ring_insufficient (the boundary alone can fail), and interior_spoke_rescues (the interior always repairs it). Honest status: a concrete verification for one coarse triangulation, not a dimension-free proof.

sections.title: The Antipodal Labelling Model
sections.summary: negL = ![2,3,0,1] is the label negation on {+1,+2,−1,−2} (Fin 4); negL_involutive and negL_free record that it is a fixed-point-free involution. V a b c = ![a,b,c,negL a,negL b,negL c] gives the six boundary labels from three free labels, with the antipodal boundary condition v_{i+3} = −v_i built in; V_antipodal decides that condition. This is the same encoding used by the sibling hexagon files SpernerTuckerHexagon and SpernerTuckerHexagonFullDoorGraph, so the model is shared across the n = 2 entries.

sections.title: Complementary Spokes and Boundary Edges
sections.summary: An edge is complementary when one endpoint's label is the antipode of the other's. The twelve edges split into six spokes centre–vᵢ (label pair (d, vᵢ)) and six boundary edges vᵢ–v_{i+1} cyclic (label pair (vᵢ, v_{i+1})). spokeCompl a b c d := ∃ i, d = negL (V a b c i) and boundaryCompl a b c := ∃ i, V a b c (i+1) = negL (V a b c i) capture 'some spoke is complementary' and 'some boundary edge is complementary'; both are given Decidable instances so the exhaustive search runs in the kernel.

sections.title: Tucker's Lemma for the Hexagon Disk
sections.summary: tucker_hexagon decides spokeCompl a b c d ∨ boundaryCompl a b c over all 4⁴ = 256 labellings — the conclusion of Tucker's lemma at n = 2: a complementary edge always exists. exists_complementary_edge unpacks it to the two endpoint labels; it is definitionally tucker_hexagon with the predicates unfolded to the raw existentials.

sections.title: The Result is 2-Dimensional: the Interior Spoke Rescues the Boundary
sections.summary: boundary_ring_insufficient decides that some boundary labelling has no complementary boundary edge (24 of the 64 boundary labellings) — so the hexagon disk does not reduce to the 1-D (S¹) statement. interior_spoke_rescues decides that in every such case a spoke is complementary for every centre label d — the concrete n = 1 → n = 2 cone step. All four #print axioms report propext / Quot.sound only.

conclusion.summary: For the standard hexagon + centre triangulation of B², tucker_hexagon proves by kernel decide over all 256 antipodal labellings that a complementary edge always exists — the actual conclusion of Tucker's lemma at n = 2, which the sixteen prior door-counting iterations had never stated on a concrete triangulation. boundary_ring_insufficient and interior_spoke_rescues then prove the result is genuinely two-dimensional: the boundary ring alone fails on 24 of 64 labellings, and the interior spoke to the centre repairs it for every centre label. Seven theorems, four definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries (propext / Quot.sound only, plain decide, no Lean.ofReduceBool).
conclusion.implications: This gives the program its first machine-checked instance of Tucker's own output — a complementary edge, the object the Borsuk–Ulam corollary ultimately consumes — at n = 2, complementing the abstract engine and sign-degree files that formalize how such an edge is FOUND. It also settles that the n = 2 case is not a disguised n = 1 one: the interior structure is doing real work, exactly as the door-counting program predicts. It does not prove Tucker for all triangulations or dimensions; the dimension-free path-following program remains the route to that.
openQuestions: Connect tucker_hexagon to the abstract door-counting engine: show the complementary edge it produces is the interior degree-1 endpoint of the almost-complementary door graph, so the concrete conclusion here is the output of SpernerTuckerInductiveTower's path-following at n = 2 rather than an independent decide.

Extend the concrete complementary-edge existence to a finer or dimension-parametric triangulation (e.g. a subdivided hexagon, or the boundary of ∂B³) and confirm the interior-cone rescue phenomenon persists, testing whether the n → n+1 step is uniform.

crossReferences.description: Parent problem entry: Tucker's lemma and Borsuk–Ulam from abstract door-counting. This entry supplies the concrete n = 2 CONCLUSION (a complementary edge exists on the hexagon disk) that the parent's abstract engines are designed to produce.

Sibling entry: the full all-signs complementary-edge DOOR GRAPH on the same hexagon triangulation is paths-and-cycles (hdoor + hsimplex). This entry proves the complementary EDGE itself always exists, the conclusion that door graph's path-following is meant to find.

Sibling entry: the dimension-free antipodal sign-degree that supplies the odd BOUNDARY SEED of the door-counting engine. This entry is the complementary concrete fact — the actual complementary edge — and shows (boundary_ring_insufficient) why the interior, not just the boundary seed, is needed at n = 2.

Grandparent entry: the verified abstract door-counting engine and TuckerTower dimension recursion whose purpose is to produce, in every dimension, the complementary edge this entry checks directly at n = 2.
